en: The most important of your affairs to me is the prayer. Whoever guards it has guarded his religion, and whoever neglects it will be more neglectful of everything else.
src: Muwatta Malik, Book of Prayer, no. 6

en: There is no share in Islam for the one who abandons the prayer.
src: Muwatta Malik, Book of Purification (attributed to Umar)

en: The world is departing and the Hereafter is approaching, and each has children. Be of the children of the Hereafter. Today is action without reckoning, tomorrow is reckoning without action.
src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Softening of Hearts (mu'allaq)

en: When you reach the evening, do not wait for the morning. When you reach the morning, do not wait for the evening. Take from your health for your illness and from your life for your death.
I have never regretted anything as I regret a day whose sun set, my life got shorter and my deeds did not grow.
src: Attributed to Ibn Mas'ud, cited by Ibn Rajab and Ibn al-Qayyim

en: O son of Adam, you are only a number of days. Whenever a day goes, a part of you goes.
src: Attributed to al-Hasan al-Basri, cited in Hilyat al-Awliya and Lata'if al-Ma'arif

en: Hold yourselves to account before you are held to account, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed for you.
src: Reported from Umar, cited by al-Tirmidhi (no. 2459) without a firm chain

en: I was deprived of standing in prayer at night for five months because of a sin I committed.
src: Attributed to Sufyan al-Thawri, cited in Hilyat al-Awliya

en: If you cannot stand at night or fast in the daytime, know that you are deprived and bound. Your sins have bound you.
src: Attributed to al-Fudayl ibn Iyad / al-Hasan al-Basri, widely cited
